title: "Session 11 --- Wet testing"

::: {.session-meta}
**Week of Nov 23** · Paired lecture: *Fixed-wing flyers*
:::

## What you do today

Immersion, underwater runs, wing trim, and control tuning in water --- the
regime the whole transmission was designed around.

## Before you arrive

| | |
|---|---|
| **Bring** | Fully waterproofed robot from [Session 10](10-waterproofing.qmd), charged 4S pack, spare crank–linkage shaft |
| **Read** | This page, and your notes from [Session 4](04-control.qmd) |

## Pre-immersion checks

- [ ] Static immersion test from Session 10 passed, robot opened and inspected dry
- [ ] Connector back-shell sealed on all unused slots
- [ ] Gearbox lubricated with CorrosionX and white lithium grease
- [ ] Watchdog enabled on the ESC (`W`) --- target drops to zero if commands stop
- [ ] Robot floats level

::: {.callout-warning}
## Low speed is where hobby ESCs fail

Water propulsion runs the motor in exactly the regime where synchronisation is
lost. If the drive stutters underwater, stop and check sensor lag compensation
before increasing current --- see [Session 4](04-control.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## To be written by the instructor

The wet-test protocol is course material and has no counterpart in the
manufacturing guide. Needed:

- Tank or venue, and supervision requirements
- Run profile: depth, duration, flap frequency sweep
- What is logged, and how it is retrieved --- SD card handling on a potted
  board is not trivial, see [PCB revisions](../reference/pcb.qmd)
- How wing trim is adjusted, and against what reference
- Cost of transport measurement procedure, since it is scored in
  [Session 12](12-competition.qmd)
- Recovery and abort procedure
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint --- TA sign-off

A completed underwater run with logged data, no water ingress on inspection
afterwards, and a recorded cost-of-transport measurement.
:::
